subject.title: perf: avoid event-loop stall during embedded_run bootstrap-context

question: Should this exact custom glob traversal and yielded bootstrap-hook scheduling become the canonical runtime behavior for existing installations?
rationale: The patch is technically coherent and well-proven, but it intentionally replaces dependency traversal behavior and introduces scheduling boundaries that can affect injected context and plugin-observable timing; repository history does not define those tradeoffs without owner intent.

options.title: Accept the runtime semantics
options.body: Land after the relevant owners confirm loaded-file parity, acceptable diagnostic and ordering differences, and the yielded hook interleaving.

options.title: Split the compatibility-sensitive parts
options.body: Land or review asynchronous guarded reads separately while isolating the custom walker and bootstrap hook scheduling into narrower follow-ups.

options.title: Require connected-run proof first
options.body: Pause landing until a live Gateway or channel scenario demonstrates responsive queued I/O during a slow bootstrap-context run.

recommendation.title: Accept the runtime semantics
recommendation.body: Land after the relevant owners confirm loaded-file parity, acceptable diagnostic and ordering differences, and the yielded hook interleaving.

likelyOwner.reason: The bootstrap hook and workspace contract history most consistently routes the final runtime compatibility decision here.
